content: A partnership has been established with the goal of fostering environmental and policy changes to encourage active living and/or healthy eating. This initiative explicitly excludes personal health programs, such as health fairs. To enable individuals to make healthier food choices, it is essential that healthy food options are both available and accessible. Families residing in low-income and minority neighborhoods often face reduced access to healthier food and beverage options compared to those living in higher-income areas. Six specific strategies have been identified to enhance the availability of healthy food and beverage choices, particularly in underserved areas. Communities should work to increase the availability of healthier food and beverage options in public service venues. Limited access to healthier food and beverage options can act as a significant barrier to healthy eating and drinking. Healthier food and beverage choices are defined as those with low energy density and reduced levels of sugar, fat, and sodium. Schools, as well as other public venues such as parks, playgrounds, swimming pools, city and county buildings, prisons, and juvenile detention centers, are critical locations for improving access to healthier foods and beverages for children and the general population. Increasing the availability of healthier options, such as fruits, vegetables, and water, in these settings may lead to greater consumption of these foods. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported insufficient evidence to determine the effectiveness of multi-component, school-based nutrition initiatives aimed at increasing fruit and vegetable intake while reducing fat and saturated fat consumption among school-aged children. However, systematic research reviews have shown a positive association between the availability of fruits and vegetables and increased consumption. Programs such as farm-to-school salad bars, which deliver produce from local farms to schools, have been shown to increase fruit and vegetable consumption among students. A two-year randomized controlled trial of a school-based environmental intervention that increased the availability of lower-fat foods in cafeteria à la carte areas demonstrated that sales of lower-fat foods increased among adolescents attending schools exposed to the intervention. This measurement evaluates whether local governments and/or public schools are implementing nutrition standards consistent with the Dietary Guidelines for Americans for foods sold in local government facilities and/or public schools. Communities that do not use the Dietary Guidelines for Americans can still meet the measurement criteria if they adhere to other standards that are similar to or stronger than the national standards. Communities should also focus on improving the affordability of healthier food and beverage options in public service venues. Healthier foods are often more expensive than less healthy alternatives, which can create a significant barrier to their purchase and consumption, particularly for low-income consumers. Healthier food and beverage options include those with low energy density and reduced calorie, sugar, fat, and sodium content. For individuals to consume healthier options, these foods must be both available and affordable. Strategies to improve the affordability of healthier foods and beverages include reducing their prices, offering discount coupons or vouchers redeemable for healthier foods, and providing bonuses tied to the purchase of healthier items. Pricing strategies create incentives for purchasing and consuming healthier foods and beverages by lowering their prices relative to less healthy options. For example, reducing the prices of healthier foods sold in vending machines and cafeterias, while increasing the prices of less healthy foods and beverages at concession stands, can encourage healthier choices. Research has demonstrated that reducing the cost of healthier foods increases their purchase. For instance, one study found that sales of fruits and carrots in high school cafeterias increased after their prices were reduced. Additionally, interventions that lowered the price of healthier, low-fat snacks in vending machines in school and workplace settings have been shown to increase the purchase of healthier snacks.
